name: Biceps curl
pattern: Elbow flexion: the forearm curls the weight up toward the shoulder while the upper arm stays still.
setup: Stand tall, feet hip width, knees soft.
Hold the weights with palms forward, arms straight by your sides.
Elbows close to your ribs, shoulders back and down.

steps.text: Arms long, elbows just in front of your hips.
Bend your elbows and bring the weight up toward your shoulders; the upper arm stays still.
Squeeze at the top with the forearm near vertical, elbows still by your sides.
Lower slowly all the way until your arms are straight.

cues.cue: Pin your elbows to your sides.
cues.why: Fixing the shoulder position is what the curl variants rely on to keep the biceps doing the work.

cues.cue: No swing: hips and back stay still.
cues.why: Body swing adds momentum and moves load to the lower back.

cues.cue: Straighten your arms fully at the bottom.
cues.why: The standard and incline curls keep high biceps activity through the whole range; the preacher curl only over a short part.

cues.cue: Palms up for biceps, thumbs up for brachioradialis.
cues.why: Hand position changes how much the brachioradialis helps; the biceps works in every grip.
Curling the wrist moves work to the forearm flexors and can irritate the wrist.

breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Curl in 1 second, lower in 2 to 3.

mistakes.name: Body swing
mistakes.looks: The hips push forward and the trunk leans back to heave the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weight; stand against a wall if needed.
mistakes.why: Momentum replaces elbow-flexor work and loads the lower back.

mistakes.name: Elbows drift forward
mistakes.looks: The elbows travel forward and up as the weight rises.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows by your sides; stop when the forearm is vertical.
mistakes.why: The front delt takes over and the biceps loses tension at the top.

mistakes.name: Half reps
mistakes.looks: The arms never straighten at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower until your elbows are straight each rep.
mistakes.why: Skipping the bottom skips the part where the biceps is longest.

safety: Elbow pain: try an EZ bar or dumbbells so the forearm can find its angle.
Preacher curls: do not drop into a fully straight elbow with a heavy load; slow the last part.

variants.change: Thumbs up (forearm 0): more brachioradialis and brachialis.
Palms down (forearm 80): brachioradialis does more; the biceps is at a disadvantage, so use less weight. Zottman: curl up palms up, lower palms down.
EZ bar: hands slightly turned in; biceps and brachioradialis activity a little higher than with dumbbells.
Drag curl: the bar slides up the body as the elbows move back behind you.
Cheat curl: a small hip drive starts the rep, then lower slowly; advanced only.
21s: 7 reps bottom half, 7 top half, 7 full.
Hold the elbow at about 90° for time.
Cable: tension stays on at the bottom and the top.
Close grip: slightly more outer (long) head.
Wide grip: slightly more inner (short) head.

subtypes.name: Preacher and spider curl
subtypes.match: preacher|spider|arm blaster|over incline bench|over exercise ball|prone
subtypes.change: Upper arm rests on a pad or hangs from a chest-down incline bench, in front of the body.

subtypes.name: Incline curl
subtypes.change: Lying back on a bench at about 45-60°, arms hanging behind the body so the biceps starts long.

subtypes.name: Concentration curl
subtypes.change: Seated, leaning forward, the back of the upper arm braced on the inner thigh; arm hangs down.

subtypes.name: Overhead cable curl
subtypes.change: Upper arms held out at shoulder height (or overhead lying under a cable); the hands curl toward the head.

subtypes.name: Hammer curl
subtypes.change: Thumbs up (forearm 0) through the whole rep; otherwise the same as the standing curl.

subtypes.name: Reverse curl
subtypes.change: Palms down (forearm 80); otherwise the same as the standing curl.

metrics.label: Elbow bend
metrics.good: 0-15 at the bottom, 120-140 at the top

motion.basis: Elbow range and shoulder fixation from oliveira2009; grip effects from kleiber2015 and marcolin2018. Shoulder blades stay still, held slightly back and down (estimate). Other angles estimated from normal standing posture.

sources.cite: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MA, Vieira TM. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med. 2009;8(1):24-29.
Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, et al. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ. 2018;6:e5165.
Kleiber T, Kunz L, Disselhorst-Klug C. Muscular coordination of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion with respect to hand position. Front Physiol. 2015;6:215.
